newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-SHORT STG TAKES BOE IN STRIDE,VOL EDGES UP.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-SHORT STG TAKES BOE IN STRIDE,VOL EDGES UP.

text.p: Short sterling options shrugged off the Bank of England's (BoE) inflation report on Wednesday, with volatility just a notch up on the day.
Activity was paltry with interest largely confined to March at-the-money strikes, and a mixed BoE report failing to inspire fresh enthusiasm in puts or calls, traders said.

The highlight of the session was 2,900 lots of March 92.00 and 93.00 strangles bought by two trade houses at a slightly higher volatility of 8.0 percent. A strangle involves buying a put, and a call at a higher strike.

"By buying the strangle you think the market will break out of this range but you're not sure which way," said Luke White, broker at Fimat Futures in London, adding that that reflected the market's mixed prospects.
A British-based bank sold March 92.75 calls at 8.23 percent volatility, traders said.

The BoE said in its quarterly report on Wednesday that a pause in monetary policy was possible as it assessed the inflation outlook. But the inflation risk was more on the upside, and more earnings rises would jeopardise the government's 2.5 percent target.
The report was largely in line with BoE views last week following a 0.25 percent rise in official rates, which it signalled could be the last one for a while.
In front month short sterling options the December 92.75 straddle was quoted at 7.1 to 7.3 percent mid vol, against 7.2 percent at the close on Tuesday.
By 1345 GMT, December futures were unchanged at 92.65 after trading in a narrow range. They shot higher after the BoE's rate action last week, but since then have trended downwards.
Traders said activity in March downside puts had thinned after a spike in demand at the beginning of the week. But volatility was cheap at current levels.
"I think it's a good time to buy (vol). If you see more of those trades then the market maker will be forced to push up vols again," said Fimat's White.

"Vol will increase slightly as we see further evidence of inflation and there is a downward pressure on gilts," said another trader, at a British brokerage. -- Clelia Oziel, International Bonds +44-171-542 8663
